- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from 14-day moving avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
- For 14+ day forecasts, model shows mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day avg is > 10% above 30-day avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overbought overcorrection.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model often ignores sentiment; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to reflect sentiment momentum.
